title: Fastly Pricing 2026: Plans, Per-TB Costs and Add-Ons
summary: Fastly pricing is based on usage, not your plan card selection. Determine your real monthly cost by calculating bandwidth, requests, and add-ons.
body_markdown:
## Every current Fastly plan with price and limits


Fastly sells three plans: a free developer tier, pay-as-you-go, and a committed contract. I couldn't verify any dollar minimum or free allowance for them, so each plan below carries a flag where a figure is missing.


Confirm every price on fastly.com/pricing before it reaches your budget.


### Fastly free developer tier pricing and limits


This is for developers testing a service or running a hobby project, and it's self-serve. Fastly describes its developer accounts in the post linked above. I couldn't verify the current free allowance, so read it off the pricing page.


Treat it as a capped trial, not a place to run production.


### Fastly pay-as-you-go plan pricing


This is the plan for most small production apps. It's self-serve, billed purely on usage, with rates published per unit. The only rates I could source are bandwidth: $0.12 to $0.08 per GB in North America and Europe, covered below, leaving request costs unavailable.


I couldn't verify whether a monthly minimum applies. If one does, it is the real cost for a tiny app.


### Fastly committed contract pricing for enterprises


This is for high-volume or security-heavy teams, and it's quote-only. The minimum, allowance and overage rate are set in negotiation, and the contract bundles CDN, WAF, DDoS, compute and support.


No published minimum exists, so I can't give you one, and no break-even calculation involving it is reliable until a quote arrives.


Ask for the minimum commitment, the overage rate and the support terms in writing, then run your own traffic through them. Pay-as-you-go gives you rates to divide by; the committed contract doesn't until someone sends one.
